la:verb:peioro.html:
pējōro, āre
pejor
, v. a. and n. (postclass.).
Act., to render worse: statum suum pejorare, opp. to meliorem facere,, tit. 18.—
Neutr., to grow worse: pejorans morbus,;

la:verb:peiero.html:
pējĕro, or, in the orig. form, perjūro (; ), and per-jĕro (; ), āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.
per-juro
,
to swear falsely, to forswear or perjure one's self.
Lit.: non enim falsum jurare pejerare (al. perjurare) est, sed quod ex animi tui sententiā juraris, sicut verbis concipitur more nostro, id non facere perjurium est,; cf.: illum verbis conceptis pejerasse,; ; : 5, 6, 2; : qui facile ac palam mentitur, pejerabit,: de aliquā re,: hic putat esse deos, et pejerat,: per consulatum pejerat Vatinius,by the consulship,.—With acc.: Stygias qui pejerat undas,by the waters of the Styx,; cf.: alii in ipso Capitolio fallunt ac fulminantem perjurant Jovem, Sillig N. cr.—Poet.: bel. lum pejerans,oath-breaking, treaty-breaking war,.—
Poet. in part. perf. pass.: jus pejeratum, a false oath (analog. to jus jurandum), : et perjuratos in mea damna deos,offended by perjury,.—
Transf., in gen., to lie (Plautin.): perge: optime hercle perjuras,: da pignus, ni nune perjures,; .
